vulnerability.title: Netty HttpPostRequestDecoder has no limit on form fields or buffered field bytes, allowing OOM

fixed_releases.verified_content: At 4.1.108.Final HttpPostRequestDecoder declares DEFAULT_MAX_FIELDS=128 and DEFAULT_MAX_BUFFERED_BYTES=1024 and passes them to both decoders; HttpPostStandardRequestDecoder.addHttpData throws TooManyFormFieldsException when bodyListHttpData.size() >= maxFields and offer throws TooLongFormFieldException when undecodedChunk.readableBytes() > maxBufferedBytes, with the same checks in the multipart decoder. At 4.1.59 none of these limits exist.

severity.source: CNA / NVD Secondary 5.3 Medium; GitHub advisory (OSV) 5.3 with database severity MODERATE

vulnerability.category_l2: Unbounded resource accumulation: the form decoders keep every field in bodyListHttpData and buffer undecoded bytes per field without limits, so a chunked POST of many small fields or one huge field exhausts the heap

description: Netty's HttpPostRequestDecoder decodes application/x-www-form-urlencoded and multipart POST bodies. At 4.1.59 neither implementation bounds the decoded state: HttpPostStandardRequestDecoder.addHttpData (lines 381-392) and the multipart addHttpData (443) append every decoded field to bodyMapHttpData and bodyListHttpData without a maximum field count, and both offer() implementations append each incoming chunk to undecodedChunk (standard 289-302, multipart 340) until a field can be decoded, without a maximum buffered size. A remote client that keeps a chunked POST open can therefore send a very large number of tiny fields, or a single field spread over many chunks, while the server keeps all of it on the heap; the decoder only discards already-consumed bytes above DEFAULT_DISCARD_THRESHOLD and applies no cap to the live form state, so the process can exhaust memory. The 4.1.108.Final fix 0d0c6ed7 adds maxFields (default 128) and maxBufferedBytes (default 1024) to both decoders and throws TooManyFormFieldsException / TooLongFormFieldException when a limit is reached.

critical_operation.description: addHttpData stores every decoded form field in bodyMapHttpData and bodyListHttpData with no count limit. The standard decoder calls it once per parsed key/value pair (parseBodyAttributesStandard at lines 422-431, parseBodyAttributes at 542-551), and the multipart decoder has the identical method at 433-444. Because the collection grows one entry per field for the lifetime of the request, a body with very many small fields exhausts the heap. The 4.1.108 fix inserts a maxFields check at the top of this method (TooManyFormFieldsException) and a maxBufferedBytes check in offer(); the 4.1.59 class has neither limit.

entry_point.description: InterfaceHttpPostRequestDecoder.offer(HttpContent): the server feeds each HTTP content chunk of a POST body to the decoder, which is where an attacker controls field count and body size.

source_crosscheck.notes: CNA, NVD and the GitHub advisory agree on the mechanism (unbounded field accumulation in HttpPostRequestDecoder), on CWE-770 and on the 5.3 Medium CVSS 3.1 vector, and all bound the affected range at 4.1.108.Final. NVD is Analyzed but carries only the GitHub-imported Secondary metric and no CPE configuration. The patch touches both the standard and multipart decoders, and the advisory's two vectors match the two missing checks (field count, buffered bytes). This root cause is distinct from the previously promoted netty entries: CVE-2021-37136 (Bzip2 decompression resource use) and CVE-2021-37137 (Snappy frame decoder resource use), CVE-2021-43797 (CRLF injection in header validation) and GHSA-wm47-8v5p-wjpj.

independent_corrections_accepted: A public reproducer does exist: the GHSA body links the Vert.x Reproducer.java gist (https://gist.github.com/vietj/f558b8ea81ec6505f1e9a6ca283c9ae3) and the reporter's fix+tests branch, and NVD SSVC records exploitation as 'poc'. The reproducer is authored by the reporter (vietj), so under the strict rule it is part of the disclosure chain, not an independent third-party reproduction, and the grade stays B.

Line-range precision: the standard offer() method spans 281-309 (not 281-310), and the multipart offer() method spans 319-357; the cited 289-302 and 340 cover the buffered-accumulation block, and the load-bearing lines (standard writeBytes 302, multipart writeBytes 340, standard addHttpData 385-391, multipart addHttpData 443, fixed checks 339-340 and 432-433) are exact.

CVE-2021-37137 is the Snappy frame decoder, not Bzip2 (CVE-2021-37136 is Bzip2); the distinctness conclusion is unchanged and the crosscheck wording was corrected.
In 4.1.108 the multipart checks are at offer 385-386 and addHttpData 482-483; the standard checks at offer 339-340 and addHttpData 432-433; constants at lines 40 and 42.
review.duplicate_check: The reviewer confirmed this is distinct from the prior netty entries using public records: CVE-2021-37136 (Bzip2 decompression, GHSA-grg4-wf29-r9vv) and CVE-2021-37137 (Snappy frame decoder, GHSA-9vjp-v76f-g363) are decompression resource issues in netty-codec; CVE-2021-43797 (GHSA-wx5j-54mm-rqqq) is header-name control-character request smuggling; GHSA-wm47-8v5p-wjpj (CVE-2021-21295) is HTTP/2 request smuggling. CVE-2024-29025 is an unbounded-allocation (CWE-770) issue in the codec-http form decoder, with no shared fix commit or code path.

limitations: Static verification only; no HTTP server, decoder or test was run and no memory exhaustion was attempted.

The issue is a resource-exhaustion DoS: it requires the application to decode POST form bodies with HttpPostRequestDecoder and to keep the connection alive while the body accumulates; the CVSS vector assumes network reachability with no privileges.
The 4.1.59 analysis cites the standard decoder as the primary location; the multipart decoder has the same missing checks and the fix patched both, but only one location row is recorded.

The default limits introduced in 4.1.108 (128 fields, 1024 buffered bytes) are a behaviour change for existing applications; they are recorded as the fixed-release content, not as a claim about the vulnerability's exploitability.

The local mirror cannot run merge-base against the depth-1 4.1.108 tag; ancestry of 0d0c6ed7 in 4.1.108.Final comes from the GitHub compare API (status ahead, behind_by 0) and from the fixed source blobs at the tag.

The reviewer identified a public reproducer (Vert.x Reproducer.java gist linked from the GHSA, plus the reporter's fix+tests branch) and NVD SSVC exploitation='poc'; because the reproducer is reporter-authored it is not treated as an independent reproduction reference and the grade remains B.

The snapshot analysis cites the standard decoder as the primary location; the multipart decoder has the same missing checks and the fix patches both, but only one location row is recorded. Method bounds per the reviewer: standard offer 281-309, multipart offer 319-357.
netty-4.1.108.Final is an annotated tag (object 1363e1bd) that dereferences to commit 3a3f9d13; the local mirror is shallow at that tag, so fix ancestry comes from the GitHub compare API.
open_questions: Whether the netty snapshot's 4.1.59.Final predates the fix is unambiguous; the exact first release that contains 0d0c6ed7 on other branches (4.0.x) was not investigated.
